svg.title: The Boundary Atlas, figure 4: the partition drill and the evidence contract
svg.desc: A vertical timeline of an inter-region partition, drawn as the best case under a stated precondition: every peer artifact was newly issued and held its full budget at the cut, because FP-1 max-ages run from each artifact's own freshness and re-fetching does not reset that clock, so in production a class can lapse at T0 itself and the order of expiry is not fixed; the boundary is inclusive, so an artifact at exactly its max-age is still within it. At T0 the link is cut: peer-sourced snapshot entries freeze at their own remaining budget while locally sourced anchors, status data, and BL-1 verdicts keep refreshing; a credential revoked by a peer issuer after the cut stays unseen for the remainder of that artifact's status window, so the base ceiling is unchanged and a tier that accepts the remaining window keeps deciding at full assurance, while a tier may override that base ceiling once the cell knows it is partitioned by tightening its own status max-age or refusing outright. Past 24 hours, peer status data is expired and checks that depend on peer revocation lose their freshness basis, so the ceiling for those checks is indeterminate, resolved per risk tier. Past 7 days, peer anchors, policy, and peer-issued BL-1 verdicts are expired too, so the per-use path disables itself wherever it depended on a peer verdict, and the derived path is available only where a qualified derived binding is installed and the anchors, status, and policy that path depends on are themselves within FP-1; otherwise the outcome is indeterminate and no allow. This does not close BL-1's issuer-visible refill channel, which runs on its published cadence regardless. At reconnect, epochs and content hashes are compared before traffic: the same epoch and hash resume; while epochs differ the intersection of allowlists sets the ceiling but conditional cargo stays blocked, so the only traffic is the staged epoch transition; and the same epoch with a different hash is an equivocating ledger, recovered by incrementing to the next epoch under the last mutually accepted authority and schema, with the equivocating epoch recorded as revoked, or by out-of-band re-provisioning where no common basis remains. Nothing is backfilled, because evidence never crossed the border. Below the timeline, the evidence contract table gives each record class its retention and the actors who may read it. Attempt evidence and the failure journal are kept two years and read by that domain's operators and auditors. Partition-access records are kept five years in whichever domain observed the refusal or failure — a request refused at the source or lost in transport never reaches the target — and are read by that same domain's operators and auditors. Observation data under rule 9 is kept thirty days and read by its own domain's operators and auditors. The BL-1 refill record set — the refill records themselves, the signed schedule manifest, each window's acceptance result, and the verdict lineage — is kept three years and read by the Issuer operator and the issuing region's auditors. Health records are kept one year and drill results three, both read by regional operators and auditors. At closure, every unexpired class is transferred to a named successor custodian in the same jurisdiction, which holds and administers each class to its own per-class expiry and deletes it there. Custody is not a reading right: the custodian inherits the keys and the administration but gains no content read by holding the store, and the readers of each class remain the inherited per-domain operators and auditors. Separately, the disposal attestation is retained for ten years and read by that jurisdiction's regulator, who is a reader of that attestation and not a reader of the evidence. Raw proofs, disclosed claims, and stable holder or credential identifiers are never recorded, and an attempt that cannot be evidenced is not allowed.
svg.text: Best case. Max-ages run from each artifact and a re-fetch does not reset
them, so in production a class can lapse at T0 and the order is not fixed.

g.text: Link cut — the cell keeps running
peer entries freeze at their own remaining budget
blind window: post-cut peer revocations unseen (residual)
checks that depend on peer revocation lose their basis
base ceiling: indeterminate there; tiers may tighten
per-use disabled where a peer verdict applied
derived only if qualified and its inputs are fresh
epochs differ: ceiling only; conditional cargo blocked
equivocation: increment under the last shared basis
The evidence contract — classes, retention, readers
never recorded: raw proofs, claims, stable holder / credential IDs
if it cannot be written: no allow, and a health record says why

svg.text: Executable here: SU-1's closure test — executable is not passed.
Partition degrades the answer, never the evidence.
